title: Private VPC upgrade preflight runbook and limited-egress compatibility matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers running Redwood Private in sealed or limited-egress VPCs need a deterministic, operator-friendly preflight that validates networking, time/auth dependencies, artifact access modes, and operatorless/offline upgrade constraints before a scheduled upgrade window. Goal: Deliver a prescriptive preflight runbook + machine-readable compatibility matrix that both SRE/ops and customers can run to determine whether an upgrade can proceed or requires a mirrored artifact/rollback plan. Out of scope: full operator rework, image signing implementation (covered elsewhere), and multi-region bandwidth provisioning. Success criteria: >95% of staged upgrades in our lab produce a deterministic PASS/FAIL with remediation hints; customers using the runbook report a measurable reduction in upgrade rollbacks during the first 90 days after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A human-readable preflight runbook exists with step-by-step checks for: DNS resolution, NTP synchronization, limited-egress mirror verification, TLS cert chain validation, KMS access test (or documented offline KMS rotation procedure), and operator health probe checks.

A2: A machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV/JSON) enumerates allowed egress hosts, ports, protocols, minimal bandwidth and latency tolerances, and artifact distribution modes (mirror, airgap bundle, bastion fetch).

A3: An automated preflight tool (CLI) executes the runbook checks and emits a PASS/FAIL plus structured remediation hints and a non-zero exit code for gating CI/CD. The tool must be able to run in airgapped mode with a pre-seeded artifact manifest.

A4: Canary validation performed in the lab across three network profiles: Full-egress (control), Limited-egress (mirror allowed to specific hosts), and No-egress (airgapped). Each profile must have documented test outcomes and rollback signal criteria.

A5: The runbook documents operatorless upgrade steps for customers who run the operator in passive mode: how to stage images, verify checksums/signatures, and trigger the local upgrade with deterministic rollback markers.
A6: Telemetry and minimum logs required for post-upgrade triage are specified and can be toggled on in restricted telemetry mode (PII redaction noted).
A7: Runbook and matrix reviewed and signed off by: Network Reliability (ENG), Security (compliance), and Solutions Engineering. Sign-offs are recorded in the ticket comments and linked artifacts.
A8: Integration tests validating preflight tool behavior are added to the private-deploy CI harness and pass in the three network profiles without flakes for 5 consecutive runs.
A9: Customer-facing runbook artifact (Confluence) and downloadable airgap bundle checklist are published in docs.redwood.ai with versioned release notes.

A10: Measurable guardrail: if preflight returns FAIL for any critical check, the upgrade automation must not progress without a manual override and documented exception approval recorded in the operator logs.

notes: Decision: We will ship the runbook and matrix first, followed by the CLI preflight tool in a patch release. Rationale: writing the checks clarifies edge cases and lets customers manually validate earlier.
Trade-off: Complete offline operatorless upgrade automation would delay delivery by 6+ weeks. We opt for documented deterministic steps plus an automated checker for common failure modes.

Risk: Bandwidth shaping and simulated partitions in lab may not capture every customer topology; mitigation includes providing a clear escalation playbook and a list of recommended mirror SaaS/VM appliances.
Implementation note: The compatibility matrix will be versioned and include a "recommended mitigation" column (e.g., local mirror, AST artifact bundle, physical media) to keep guidance prescriptive.
